core_claim.quote: Experiences of emotion and mood, which seem central to selfhood, may depend on interoceptive inferences – probabilistic best-guesses about the causes of sensory inputs signalling the physiological condition of the body

source.citation: Seth AK. Conscious artificial intelligence and biological naturalism. Behavioral and Brain Sciences 49, e315 (published online 2025-04-21)

prediction.statement: Brain regions that handle signals from inside the body, the anterior insula above all, respond less to body signals that were well predicted and more when the prediction is violated.

first_stated.passage: A second basic prediction is that the AIC, as well as other areas involved in interoceptive processing, should show responses consistent with interoceptive predictive coding. For example, by analogy with studies of repetition suppression, AIC should show reduced responses for well predicted interoceptive signals and enhanced responses when expectations are violated.

source.citation: Seth AK, Suzuki K, Critchley HD. An interoceptive predictive coding model of conscious presence. Frontiers in Psychology 2:395 (2011 volume)

prediction.test_for: Anterior insula (or another body-signal region) responds less to a body signal, or to a signal locked to one, when it is predictable, and more when it breaks the prediction.
prediction.test_against: No reduction for predictable body signals and no increase for violated ones, in a design that finds such effects for comparable outside-world signals.

study.name: Brain imaging while people learned to predict when breathing would become hard (7-tesla fMRI)

source.citation: Harrison OK, Köchli L, Marino S, Luechinger R, Hennel F, Brand K, Hess AJ, Frässle S, Iglesias S, Vinckier F, Petzschner FH, Harrison SJ, Stephan KE. Interoception of breathing and its relationship with anxiety. Neuron 109(24):4080 onward, 2021

passages.text: In this Breathing Learning Task (BLT), 80 trials were performed where on each trial two visual cues were paired with either an 80% or 20% chance of a subsequent inspiratory resistive load.

source.citation: Harrison OK, Köchli L, Marino S, Luechinger R, Hennel F, Brand K, Hess AJ, Frässle S, Iglesias S, Vinckier F, Petzschner FH, Harrison SJ, Stephan KE. Interoception of breathing and its relationship with anxiety. Neuron 109(24):4080 onward, 2021

passages.text: In contrast, aIns, ACC, MFG, and the periaqueductal gray (PAG) demonstrated significant activations with overall prediction error values (i.e., averaged across trials with positive and negative prediction errors; Figure 4 B).

passages.text: Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), anterior insula (aIns), anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), and middle frontal gyrus (MFG) all demonstrated significant deactivations with overall prediction certainty (i.e., averaged across trials with positive and negative prediction certainty; Figure 4 A).
